chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Bureyd, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man who accepts (rent for) the land with dinars or with dirhams, he (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay land rent in gold or silver coins according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the use of contemporary currency standards—gold dinars and silver dirhams—for land rent, reflecting the practical economic norms of the early Islamic period. It underscores the flexibility in Islamic commercial law regarding the medium of exchange, provided the value is agreed upon, a principle that later jurists extended to various forms of money. This ruling highlights the Imam's emphasis on removing unnecessary hardship in contractual agreements.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al hajjal, from Sa’albat Bin Maymoun, from Bureyd, 
from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the man who accepts (the rent for) the land with the Dinars or with the Dirhams. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Tha’labah ibn Maymun from Burayd who has said
the following: “About the case of a man who accepts dinar or dirham for (the rent of) land, abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, has said, ‘It is not unlawful.’”
